clinician.trajectory_summary: A 25-year-old Asian woman with lupus (discoid rash and arthralgia) on prednisone 15 mg daily presented to the emergency room with a 6-day history of acute right-sided sharp headaches (10/10 severity, intermittent, lasting seconds, occurring multiple times daily) with occasional spread to the right neck and pulsating quality. She also reported brief lower back spasmic-type pain. Neurologic examination was unremarkable with no migrainous features or trigeminal autonomic symptoms. She had self-discontinued mycophenolate 1 week prior to admission. Initial laboratory workup revealed an isolated elevated PTT (74 seconds) with normal CBC, normal chemistry panel, normal liver panel, normal INR, and normal urine toxicology. A mixing study failed to correct with a 1:1 ratio to plasma, indicating the presence of an inhibitor. Subsequent testing revealed an undetectable factor 8 level, consistent with acquired hemophilia A. Brain MRI demonstrated bilateral infracerebellar and right pre-pontine extra-axial hematomas, explaining the patient's headache localization and character. The patient was treated with recombinant factor 7a and rituximab, with repeat imaging showing resolving hematomas. The clinical trajectory supports acquired hemophilia A (factor 8 inhibitor) as the final diagnosis, likely precipitated by lupus disease activity and mycophenolate discontinuation.
